clusters.name: User Authentication Strategy
clusters.description: Authentication mechanisms and credential-handling choices that control how riders establish identity, distinct from broader data-protection controls.

relations.rationale: Authentication choices determine which user identities may initiate rental, payment, and data-access operations.

values.label: Email-password authentication
values.description: Authenticate riders with email and password credentials, transmitted securely and stored using protected credential-handling mechanisms.

clusters.name: Data Protection Strategy
clusters.description: Confidentiality mechanisms for data during transport and storage, distinct from identity verification and application workflow decisions.

relations.rationale: Protection requirements constrain payment integration designs because third-party transaction data must remain secure in transit and at rest.

values.label: End-to-end data encryption
values.description: Apply end-to-end encryption to user and transaction data both while moving between components and while stored.

clusters.name: Bike Discovery Strategy
clusters.description: Spatial query and filtering choices that determine how the platform identifies available bikes near a rider.

values.label: Radius-bounded geospatial discovery
values.description: Use geospatial proximity filtering to return bikes within the specified bounded search radius, supporting nearby-bike discovery.

clusters.name: Rental Lifecycle Control
clusters.description: Control-flow models for rider navigation, bike scanning, unlocking, and rental progression, distinct from notification delivery.

relations.rationale: Lifecycle transitions produce state changes that must be disseminated to interfaces and other interested components.

values.label: State-machine rental workflow
values.description: Represent navigation, scanning, unlocking, and rental progression as explicit states managed by a state machine.

clusters.name: Rental State Dissemination
clusters.description: Runtime event-propagation mechanisms that keep interfaces and components synchronized with changing rental states.

relations.rationale: State dissemination is driven by rental lifecycle transitions and therefore accompanies lifecycle control choices.

values.label: Observer-based real-time updates
values.description: Use an Observer-based notification mechanism to propagate rental-state changes, including timing or scheduling-aware updates, to UI components.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The encryption-related codes map to Dimension 2 (Data Protection Strategy), which already covers end-to-end encryption in transit and at rest, as well as protection of sensitive transaction data. The Observer-based notifications, real-time UI propagation, and scheduling-aware dissemination map to Dimension 5 (Rental State Dissemination), whose axis is runtime event propagation for rental-state changes. The email-password authentication, secure transmission, and secure credential storage codes are covered by Dimension 1 (User Authentication Strategy) and, where applicable, by Dimension 2 for transport/storage protection. The geospatial proximity filtering and radius-bounded discovery codes are covered by Dimension 3 (Bike Discovery Strategy). The payment facade, delegation, provider adapter normalization, and common internal payment interface codes all fall under Dimension 6 (Payment Integration Strategy). The Builder/report export codes are covered by Dimension 7 (Usage Reporting Strategy). The state-machine/navigation/unlocking/lifecycle tracking codes are covered by Dimension 4 (Rental Lifecycle Control). No open code introduces a genuinely new architectural axis beyond the existing dimensions for the CityBike use case.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. Pricing strategy, rental duration tracking, pre-expiry reminders, and Command-pattern rental operations map directly to dimensions 8, 4, and 5. Identity, contact, credential capture, optional location data, secure form handling, input validation, manual session termination, and verification-code validity are covered by dimensions 1 and 2. Repository-based data access and operational dashboard/analytics fit dimensions 9 and 10. The boundary statements about keeping notifications outside pricing or command decomposition do not introduce a new architectural axis; they reinforce existing separations already represented by the pricing, lifecycle, dissemination, and data-access dimensions. No genuinely new concept relevant to CityBike's architecture appears uncovered.
